Logical reading and tab order depend on document structure. Complex graphics, tables and footnotes can require correction after conversion; correct source structure and actual reading-order testing matter.

recommended_path: Keep the reviewed visual editions intact while preparing a separately named semantic reading edition from canonical HTML and current manifest, with source hashes and explicit source coverage.

Refresh stale metadata, seven-part/current-reading bindings, durable licensed fonts, image-family handling and actual alt text. Preserve headings, lists, figures/captions, table header associations and source-note return links; do not flatten meaningful material into page screenshots.

Generate tags and outline in Chromium as the prototype already supports. Include covers within the semantic generation or explicitly validate any subsequent assembly. Mark decorative ornaments appropriately, while retaining credit notes and meaningful image descriptions.

Inspect final structure tree, ParentTree and marked-content references, figure alt text, header scopes, annotation object associations and internal targets. Compare extracted Unicode and rendered Odia shaping against source; successful visual shaping does not establish correct searchable/readable Unicode.

Check lang=or passage semantics in the output tree. If browser output still loses language, repair only correctly identified Odia structure spans using a validated tagging/remediation workflow; a global language flag or guessed whole-paragraph relabel is insufficient.

Validate reading order and coverage throughout the complete book, then manually test representative complex chapters with assistive technology, keyboard citation/return and table navigation. Only describe tested capabilities; reserve PDF/UA claims for complete applicable validation.
feasible_this_pass: Document the implementation route and unresolved gates.
Retain current HTML reading routes as the existing alternative format, without asserting their complete AT certification.

requires_followup: Updated prototype implementation and source-bound generation.
Odia structure-language investigation and any verified remediation.

Full visual regression on final tagged artifact; current book layout approval cannot transfer automatically.
limitations: No new binaries built or inspected in this task; historical structural counts are explicitly retained evidence.

No promise that Chromium alone resolves language tagging or all semantic coverage.
